The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, on Tuesday, inaugurated three Liquefied to Compressed Natural Gas facilities in Kano, describing it as a symbol of energy equity and a major milestone in the Federal Government’s ‘Decade of Gas’ initiative. The facilities were developed by Rolling Energy Limited with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund. They comprise a 300,000-standard cubic metres per day Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas distribution hub and a retail station at Tamburawa, Dawakin Kudu Local Government Area, as well as a 21,000-standard cubic metres per day LCNG daughter and retail station at Hotoro, in Tarauni Local Government Area. Speaking at the commissioning, Ekpo said the projects demonstrated the Federal Government’s determination to translate its gas policies into infrastructure that would deliver tangible benefits to Nigerians. “We must move from policies to projects, from plans to infrastructure, and from gas reserves beneath our soil to affordable energy that actually reaches our homes, businesses, industries and transportation systems,” he said. Add us to your Preferred Sources The minister said the facilities would deepen gas penetration in Kano and neighbouring areas, provide cleaner energy alternatives, support businesses and transportation, stimulate economic activities and create opportunities for residents. “What we commission today is more than three pieces of infrastructure. It is the Renewed Hope made tangible: gas infrastructure delivered, energy brought closer to the people, businesses empowered, and new economic opportunities created,” Ekpo said. He explained that the Tamburawa hub would provide LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution services, including supplies to daughter stations, while the retail outlets would bring gas closer to end users. FG unveils three gas stations in Kano to boost CNG adoption Kano gov unveils N50,000 grants for 5,200 women Varsity to secure NUC’s AI approval Ekpo said the role of the MDGIF was critical to developing the domestic gas sector, noting that government must attract private capital to build the infrastructure needed to expand access to gas. “Government cannot stop at formulating good policies. We must catalyse the private capital and infrastructure required to translate those policies into benefits that Nigerians can see, use and feel,” he said. Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismail Ahmed, said the commissioning reflected growing investment in CNG infrastructure across the country. Ahmed, who was represented at the event by his Special Adviser on Technical Training and Capacity Building Mr. Omoh Imoukhede, said the expansion of refuelling facilities were necessary to support the increasing conversion of vehicles to CNG, particularly in commercial centres such as Kano, where many residents depend on affordable transportation for their livelihoods. “Conversion without refuelling infrastructure will not deliver the transition we want. The two must grow together,” he said. He added that convenient and reliable refuelling stations would encourage commercial drivers and fleet operators to adopt CNG, while the government would continue to prioritise affordability, availability and safety.
